bug_semantics: A user permitted to create a pod can supply a crafted checkpoint archive or checkpoint OCI image whose untrusted status.dump contains cdi.k8s.io annotations naming a device from a host CDI specification. CRImportCheckpoint restores those annotations into the new container configuration, and the normal Linux create path parses them with WithCDI and applies the matching CDI edits to the OCI spec. With CDI enabled and a matching host specification, this can add device nodes and host mounts without the Kubernetes resource-allocation/device-plugin authorization path.
flaw_origin: The initial CRI/Kubernetes container-restore implementation trusted checkpoint-carried ContainerStatus.annotations as authoritative create-time metadata. It copied the complete map from status.dump into meta.Config.Annotations, changing only a few Kubernetes bookkeeping values and performing no CDI-namespace validation before createContainer consumed the annotations.
ai_marker: absent — git cat-file commit 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd shows human author and committer Adrian Reber <areber@redhat.com>; the only message trailer is Signed-off-by: Adrian Reber <areber@redhat.com>, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other commit-object AI marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-33vj-92qq-66hc identifies CVE-2026-53492, the checkpoint CDI-annotation-smuggling mechanism, the prerequisite of enabled CDI plus a matching host CDI specification, affected ranges >=2.1.0 <2.1.9, >=2.2.0 <2.2.5, and >=2.3.0 <2.3.2, and patched versions 2.1.9, 2.2.5, and 2.3.2.

BIC source evidence: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd and https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd/internal/cri/server/container_checkpoint_linux.go#L237-L368. At line 237 CRImportCheckpoint reads checkpoint-controlled status.dump into ContainerStatus; line 255 assigns containerStatus.GetAnnotations() to originalAnnotations; the intervening code only rewrites selected Kubernetes bookkeeping entries; line 368 assigns the resulting whole map to meta.Config.Annotations.

Attack-path sink: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd/internal/cri/server/container_create_linux.go#L103-L104 passes config.Annotations to customopts.WithCDI when CDI is enabled. internal/cri/opts/spec_linux.go parses CDI annotations and invokes cdispec.WithCDIDevices, which applies the host CDI specification's device edits.

History proof: git log --all -SoriginalAnnotations --follow -- internal/cri/server/container_checkpoint_linux.go and git log -L 255,368:internal/cri/server/container_checkpoint_linux.go 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd both identify 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd as the commit that introduced the vulnerable annotation-copying block. Earlier commit f25770e48d666edb63eb4061bf47242ebc1cf22d only created the checkpoint file for checkpointing and did not introduce restore-time annotation trust.

Direct-parent verification: git grep at 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd finds CRImportCheckpoint at internal/cri/server/container_checkpoint_linux.go:110, originalAnnotations := containerStatus.GetAnnotations() at :255, and meta.Config.Annotations = originalAnnotations at :368. The same git grep against direct parent 07dd4ccf3599d4c22ee679b36fda3a17f8801cc2 returns no matches for any of those three expressions. Parent: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/07dd4ccf3599d4c22ee679b36fda3a17f8801cc2.

Smallest-public-commit proof: 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd is a one-parent feature commit and the second parent of merge 9b552d441582d71b7fd322c0b9f2c7c23b26b729 (Merge pull request #10365), not a merge/release/backport or an unreconstructed squash aggregate. PR and merge references: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/10365 and https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/9b552d441582d71b7fd322c0b9f2c7c23b26b729.

Canonical direct fix: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/861ffc1097685f9ecf13adaa381aca5fdf7ef0b4 changes CRImportCheckpoint to call filterAndMergeAnnotations, which drops keys exactly equal to cdi.k8s.io or prefixed cdi.k8s.io/ before assigning restored annotations, while retaining the intended bookkeeping merge. Release backports are 91d7471e2cc7113c31dbcc62007756ba88f8cf9f for v2.3.2, be8460656b84c4a1a4b244a03801e9fff1e914d3 for v2.2.5, and 02045fd4696d21db11767226ff14576522809066 for v2.1.9: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/91d7471e2cc7113c31dbcc62007756ba88f8cf9f, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/be8460656b84c4a1a4b244a03801e9fff1e914d3, and https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/02045fd4696d21db11767226ff14576522809066.

Version-boundary verification: git merge-base --is-ancestor shows the BIC is absent from v2.0.7 but present in v2.1.0, v2.1.8, v2.1.9, v2.2.0, v2.2.4, v2.2.5, v2.3.0, v2.3.1, and v2.3.2. git grep at v2.0.7 finds neither the restore annotation source nor the filter; v2.1.0/v2.1.8, v2.2.0/v2.2.4, and v2.3.0/v2.3.1 contain originalAnnotations := containerStatus.GetAnnotations() but no filterAndMergeAnnotations; first-patched v2.1.9, v2.2.5, and v2.3.2 each contain filterAndMergeAnnotations. Ancestry also places 02045fd4696d21db11767226ff14576522809066 in v2.1.9, be8460656b84c4a1a4b244a03801e9fff1e914d3 in v2.2.5, and 91d7471e2cc7113c31dbcc62007756ba88f8cf9f in v2.3.2.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins with checkpoint content under the pod creator's control. The restore path deserializes status.dump, preserves its annotation map, and substitutes that map for the pod's create-time annotations. Because the ordinary Linux create path interprets cdi.k8s.io annotations and applies the referenced host CDI edits, restored metadata crosses an authorization boundary and bypasses Kubernetes device allocation. Pickaxe and line history trace the first flawed mechanism to the original restore feature commit 9e6beafd53919eecd1fb650a76332002cf4c84dd; its direct parent contains no CRImportCheckpoint or vulnerable annotation-copy lines, and the feature commit is a single normal PR member commit rather than a merge/backport/squash requiring decomposition. The BIC is absent before v2.1 and present at each affected-range lower bound. Canonical fix 861ffc1097685f9ecf13adaa381aca5fdf7ef0b4 filters the CDI namespace, and its three release-line backports appear exactly at v2.1.9, v2.2.5, and v2.3.2. Under BIC-only attribution, the BIC commit object is human-authored/committed and has no AI marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
